A.title: Thread Under the Boot
A.text: Each step plucks a thread. Somewhere below, something feels it; walk slow and the web lets you; run and it knows. I ran, once.

Y.title: The Loom Hall Ledger
Y.text: Thirty looms, bone frames, black thread. The weavers made cloth for the dead; they were paid in grain. The last bolt on the oldest loom was never cut; do not cut it.

R.title: A Second Pulse
R.text: Spun silk carries a beat, if you press it to your wrist. Slower than yours; match it and your own heart slows too. The weavers sat like this for hours; try it before a fight.

G.title: Silkworm Shelves
G.text: Shelves of worms, still alive, still eating. Someone feeds them; we never found who; take nothing from the shelves. The cocoon store is the safe place for supplies.

M.title: Weavers' Rest, Cot Count
M.text: Eleven cots, ten blankets. One cot unmade. One weaver did not rest; she went down to the pattern room and did not come back.

O.title: Pattern Library Shelf
O.text: The library holds the patterns of the web; each is a map of one floor; a weaver who reads them could walk without waking the Queen. I tried. I woke the Queen.

U.title: Clean Corner
U.text: There is a corner with no web; every other corner is thick. Somebody sweeps it; do not ask who. Sleep there if you must, and keep one hand on a blade.

X.title: The Weaver Queen
X.text: She is not a spider. She was a woman once, a weaver of the first age, and she wove herself in. She still sings while she works; do not listen to the end of the song.
